thread:
maria: FYI — ACME prod reports a bunch of threshold alerts for error-rate that look spurious. Graph shows spikes exactly at minute boundaries.
kevin: link to the alert / rule id?
maria: rule=rule-3042, dashboard https://console/redwood/acme/errors (customer sent screenshot). They say it started after the last ingest rollout.
alerts-bot: Alert rule-3042 fired 14 times in the past 40m across svc-a, svc-b. avg latency 110ms. :rotating_light:
josh: Do we have the raw metric buckets? this smells like bucket alignment/rollup drift.
maria: I pulled the raw timeseries. See excerpt below.

maria: ```
# from timeseries-store
timestamp, svc, error_count
2026-02-27T07:59:45Z, svc-a, 6
2026-02-27T08:00:00Z, svc-a, 0
2026-02-27T08:00:15Z, svc-a, 105
2026-02-27T08:01:00Z, svc-a, 2
```

sophie: hmm that 15s offset is new. We usually align rollups to whole minute. recent ingest change added optional jitter/offset for alignment to improve write clustering.
kevin: where was that flag toggled? I remember we shipped a change to rollup alignment to support sub-minute buckets for high-tps customers.

josh: quick repro: run aggregation with different bucket offsets and compare counts.

oncall-sre: ran a quick query:

oncall-sre: ```
# query A: align 0s
SELECT sum(error_count) FROM metrics
WHERE service='svc-a' AND time >= now() - 5m
GROUP BY time(1m, 0s)
-- result: bucket at 08:00 contains 0 errors

# query B: align 15s
SELECT sum(error_count) FROM metrics
WHERE service='svc-a' AND time >= now() - 5m
GROUP BY time(1m, 15s)
-- result: bucket at 08:00 contains 105 errors
```

sophie: so the same events end up in different minute buckets based on alignment. Our alert rule uses aggregation window=5m but the evaluation engine is aligning to the server-local offset (15s) while the dashboard chart aligns to UTC minute — mismatch.
kevin: that explains misfires. If the alert window slices cross the boundary differently than the chart, threshold comparisons will flip around the boundary.

maria: customer-facing impact: they see the chart noise and get fired alerts. They escalated to support.
kevin: short term mitigation: change the rule evaluation to use a fixed alignment (0s) or increase evaluation interval to 1m to avoid boundary jitter.
sophie: I can push a change to alerting config: default align_to=0 for all rules unless explicitly set. small config change, no code change.

josh: long term: we should standardize the rollup alignment across ingestion, query engine, and alert evaluator. probably store an "alignment_offset" per metric when rollup happens and surface it in query planner.
kevin: agree. I'll open a ticket and schedule a canary deploy for the config change.

maria: I told ACME support team we paused rule-3042 for the ACME org for 1h and will follow up. They were relieved.

oncall-sre: putting repro steps in the ticket: 1) create sample metric with timestamps at +15s, 2) run GROUP BY time(1m,0s) vs time(1m,15s), 3) compare counts and see alert flip.

sophie: for immediate ops: created a temporary rule override: set evaluation_period=2 and align_to=0 for customer-scoped rules. rolling out now.
kevin: I'll monitor alert churn post-change and follow up. thanks all. :thumbsup:
alerts-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1155 assigned to kevin.
